doc.title: Bruce Johnstone interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2013

title: Live at Jimmy's: the eight a.m. recording with Maynard
summary: Playing the live album at Jimmy's after an all-night drive while Maynard, recovering from jaw surgery, played unexpectedly; mouthpiece and reeds on the recording.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Well I have a couple of the different sides of what you do, and I just wanted to —
Yup. Eight o’clock in the morning.
This was eight o’clock in the morning?

Yup. Maynard had had some major tooth surgery, had part of his jaw taken out. His dentist was traveling with him to make sure that he didn’t play. So for the first two weeks of his tour Maynard didn’t play a note. We played in Boston the night before until about two in the morning, then we drove to New York. Nobody slept. And we went into this club, Jimmy’s, at eight o’clock in the morning, and then did a sound check and then straight into it. And everything on that recording was live, one take. And when we opened up with “Blue Birdland” the deal was Maynard was going to overdub later. And we were playing the theme and all of a sudden Maynard grabbed his horn and went [scats] and the dentist’s face went white. And Maynard played with no warm-up, strong as I’ve ever heard him. And the man was amazing.
I think Thad Jones-Mel Lewis, they did a record like that with Joe Williams, where they were up all night and they just went into the studio.

Yeah. Sometimes you get that momentum building up to that moment — rather than he’d go in, have breakfast, and everything’s calm and he said, “hello, good morning everybody,” and they all have had coffee, and the spirit is not there.
Yeah. You do a cool thing here.
That’s great. To get some tone to go with it, I think is hard.
The mouthpiece I was using on that was a Meyer ten, and I was using number five reeds. Of course in my declining years I’ve gone down one strength in reeds.
Yes. It’s not bad to go down. Wow.
